Blaszczak\\n\\nThe  MCA  analysis  also  showed  that  different  determinants  are  strongly  interconnected.\\nDeveloping a security policy is a key starting point, on which other activities, such as encryption\\nor audits, are based. Educational activities, in turn, play a supporting role, increasing the overall\\neffectiveness of the remaining elements of the security strategy. The results also indicate the\\nneed  to  integrate  technical  and  organizational  activities,  which  allows  for  a  more\\ncomprehensive and effective approach to data protection in outsourcing processes.\\nIn summary, the research confirms that effective data security management requires a multi-\\nfaceted approach, taking into account both technological and organizational elements. Security\\npolicy, regular audits and the use of advanced technologies such as encryption, supported by\\nbuilding  awareness  among  employees,  are  of  key  importance.  Such  an  approach  allows  to\\nminimize the risk and ensure effective data protection within the framework of outsourcing\\ncooperation.\\nTo effectively manage data security in outsourcing processes, companies should focus on\\nseveral key activities. First of all, it is necessary to create a comprehensive data security policy\\nthat  will  become  the  basis  for  all  security  practices.  Such  a  policy  should  clearly  define\\nstandards, procedures and responsibilities both within the organization and in relations with\\noutsourcing partners. It is equally important to conduct regular security audits, which allow for\\nearly detection of gaps and potential threats. These audits should be carried out systematically\\nand take into account both technological and organizational aspects, which allows for a full\\nassessment  of  the  effectiveness  of  the  implemented  actions.  Commissioning  audits  to\\nindependent entities can additionally increase the objectivity of the results.\\nImplementing advanced technologies, such as data encryption, should be a priority for every\\norganization. Encryption protects data from unauthorized access, especially when transferring\\ninformation between a company and an outsourcing service provider. It is important that this\\ntechnology  is  used  consistently  and  adapted  to  the  specifics  of  the  company’s  operations.\\nThe role of employee education cannot be forgotten either. Regular data security training is\\ncrucial  because  it  allows  not  only  to  increase  knowledge  about  threats,  but  also  to  build\\nawareness of responsibility for protecting information. Employees should not only know the\\nbasic  principles  of  security,  but  also  be  able  to  recognize  more  advanced  threats,  such  as\\nattempted social engineering attacks.\\nIt is also important to develop transparent relationships with outsourcing service providers.\\nBuilding trust through clear communication of requirements and joint planning of data security\\nactivities can significantly increase the effectiveness of the actions taken. It is important that\\nthe  cooperation  is  grounded  in  detailed  agreements  regulating  data  protection  standards,\\nand their compliance is systematically monitored. An approach that combines technological,\\norganizational and educational aspects allows companies to manage data protection risks more\\neffectively. Implementing these activities not only strengthens security, but also builds trust\\namong customers and partners, which translates into the stability and long-term development\\nof the company.\\n\\n## [PDF page 169]\\n\\nDeterminants of data security…  169\\n\\nThe key studies highlight important determinants of data security in outsourcing, such as\\nsecurity  policies,  encryption,  audits,  and  employee  education.  However,  the  research  has\\nlimitations, including reliance solely on quantitative methods, lack of consideration for specific\\nsectors  (e.g.,  medical,  financial),  and  omission  of  the  dynamic  development  of  new\\ntechnologies like artificial intelligence or  blockchain. Additionally, the uniform sample and\\nrestriction to MCA analysis do not  fully  capture the complexity of the issue. Despite these\\nweaknesses, the studies provide valuable practical insights and a solid foundation for further\\nexploration.\\nThe new knowledge brought by the conducted research includes a detailed identification\\nand analysis of data security determinants in outsourcing processes, such as security policies,\\ndata  encryption,  audits,  and  employee  awareness-building.  The  study  demonstrated  that  the\\neffective and integrated implementation of these elements significantly reduces risks related to\\ndata loss or unauthorized access. One key conclusion is the necessity of developing a coherent\\nsecurity policy, which serves as the foundation for other actions, such as audits and education.\\nIt was also shown that data encryption is perceived as a crucial element of technical protection,\\nthough  its  effectiveness  may  be  limited  by  implementation  costs  and  technological\\nrequirements.\\nAnother  important  finding  is  the  role  of  employee  education  in  minimizing  the  risk  of\\nhuman  errors,  which  enhances  the  effectiveness  of  other  protective  measures.  Moreover,\\nthe  analysis  of  interdependencies  among  security  determinants  highlights  the  need  for\\na  comprehensive  approach  that  integrates  technological,  organizational,  and  educational\\naspects. The conclusions provide organizations with practical guidelines for improving data\\nsecurity in outsourcing and serve as a basis for further research in this area.\\nThe  conducted  research  is  of  significant  importance  for  the  practice  of  data  security\\nmanagement in outsourcing processes, particularly in the context of increasing cyber threats\\nand  tightening  legal  regulations.  Its  findings  contribute  new  knowledge  about  the  key\\ndeterminants of effective data protection, enabling organizations to better understand which\\nactions are most effective in minimizing risks.\\nThe  impact  of  the  research  on  the  broader  field  includes  supporting  organizations  in\\ndeveloping more advanced data protection strategies that can be tailored to various sectors and\\nspecific industry needs. Moreover, highlighting the importance of elements such as security\\npolicies, encryption, audits, and education provides valuable insights for both practitioners and\\nfurther  scientific  studies.  The  information  obtained  can  be  used  to  develop  comprehensive\\nsecurity  standards  applicable  across  different  organizations.  The  findings  can  also  serve  as\\na  starting  point  for  further  exploration  of  the  topic,  particularly  in  the  context  of  dynamic\\ntechnological  changes  such  as  the  development  of  artificial  intelligence  and  blockchain.\\nAdditionally,  this  research  may  inspire  analyses  in  specific  economic  sectors,  where  data\\nprotection issues are of particular importance, such as the financial, medical, or educational\\nsectors.\\n\\n## [PDF page 170]\\n\\n170  D. Conclusions\\n\\nComparing  the  results  of  the  conducted  studies  with  the  findings  of  other  researchers,\\none can notice both similarities and differences in the perception of the determinants of data\\nsecurity in the context of outsourcing. A study published in \\"Issues in Information Systems\\"\\nindicated that despite concerns about security, some of the largest technology companies locate\\ntheir operations in India, trusting the assurances of local service providers about data protection\\n(Ghosh, Scott, 2008). Other sources emphasize the importance of physical data protection and\\nquality management systems in the context of outsourcing, which is consistent with the results\\nof the discussed studies, which indicate the importance of developing a security policy and\\nregular audits (Infinit-O Global, 2022).\\nThe literature also draws attention to the need to use advanced cryptographic technologies\\nto  ensure  secure  access  to  data  stored  in the  cloud,  which  corresponds  to  the  results  of the\\ndiscussed studies, emphasizing the importance of data encryption (Bertino, 2009). Furthermore,\\na  review  of  the  literature  on  secure  outsourcing  of  computations  indicates  the  need  to  use\\nvarious security methods to cope with the threats associated with transferring IT functions to\\nexternal entities (Wang et al., 2015).\\nIn the context of IT outsourcing, other studies identify factors influencing organizations ’\\ndecisions to outsource IT security functions, emphasizing the importance of both managerial\\nand legal aspects (Arshad et al., 2022). Furthermore, the analysis of risks related to outsourcing\\nand  offshoring  services  indicates  the  need  to  apply  preventive  and  corrective  measures  to\\nminimize potential threats (Nassimbeni et al., 2012). The results of the conducted research are\\nconsistent  with  the  literature  on  the  subject,  emphasizing  the  importance  of  developing\\na security policy, using advanced cryptographic technologies, and regular audits to ensure data\\nsecurity  in  outsourcing  processes.  At  the  same  time,  differences  in  the  perception  of  some\\naspects, such as employee education, may result from the specificity of the studied samples and\\nthe cultural and organizational context.\\nThe  limitations  of  research  based  on  the  analysis  of  data  security  determinants  in\\noutsourcing  processes  resulted  from  several  factors.  First,  the  research  was  based  on  data\\ncollected  using  a  survey,  which  limits  the  possibility  of  in-depth  qualitative  analysis.\\nRespondents could interpret the questions in a subjective way, which potentially influenced the\\nresults. In addition, the method used does not allow for full capture of the complex relationships\\nbetween  variables  in  the  dynamically  changing  outsourcing  environment,  especially  in  the\\ncontext of cultural and technological differences between companies.\\nThe second limitation was the uniform sample of 723 respondents, which, although large in\\nnumber, did not fully reflect the diversity of entities using outsourcing. The sample did not\\ninclude specific sectors, such as the medical or financial industries, which may have different\\ndata security challenges. Additionally, the lack of data on the geographic origin of respondents\\n\\n## [PDF page 171]\\n\\nDeterminants of data security…  171\\n\\nlimited the ability to analyze the impact of regional factors on the results. Another limitation\\nwas the lack of consideration of dynamic changes in data security technologies, which could\\nhave influenced the perception of some security determinants. Therefore, the results may not\\nfully  reflect  current  technological  trends  and  innovations,  such  as  the  use  of  artificial\\nintelligence or advanced encryption methods.\\nFinally,  the  study’s  limitations  also  related  to  the  choice  of  MCA  analysis  as  the  main\\nanalytical  method.  Although  it  allows  for  the  identification  of  patterns  and  relationships\\nbetween  variables,  its  results  are  more  difficult  to  interpret  in  the  case  of  more  complex\\nrelationships.  The  lack  of  complementary  statistical  analyses,  such  as  regression  or  cluster\\nanalysis, may have limited the fullness of conclusions drawn from the obtained data.\\nIn conclusion, the limitations of the study result mainly from the adopted methodology,\\nsample characteristics and the lack of consideration of the dynamically changing technological\\nenvironment. However, the results constitute an important starting point for further research,\\nwhich can deepen and extend the conclusions, taking into account a broader context and more\\ndiverse  analytical  tools.  Future  research  directions  may  focus  on  a  more  comprehensive\\nunderstanding of the determinants of data security in the context of various economic sectors.\\nAn important area for exploration is the analysis of specific industry requirements, such as\\nhealthcare, the financial sector or education, where data protection is of particular importance\\ndue to its sensitivity and legal regulations. The research may also take into account geographical\\nand cultural differences in the perception of data security, which would allow for adapting the\\nstrategy to regional needs and requirements.\\nAn  important  aspect  of  further  research  may  be  the  analysis  of  dynamic  changes  in\\ntechnologies  related  to  data  protection,  such  as  the  development  of  artificial  intelligence,\\nblockchain or advanced encryption methods. Examining their impact on the perception of data\\nsecurity and the effectiveness of the practices used could provide valuable tips for organizations\\nlooking for modern solutions in this area. Another area to explore is the role of education and\\nemployee  awareness  in  the  context  of  minimizing  the  risk  associated  with  human  errors.\\nResearch could focus on assessing the effectiveness of various training methods and identifying\\nbest practices in building a security culture in organizations using outsourcing.\\nIt is also possible to deepen the analysis of cooperation between companies and outsourcing\\nservice  providers,  especially  in  terms  of  building  trust  and  transparency  in  business\\nrelationships.  Research  could  include  aspects  of  contract  negotiations,  mechanisms  for\\nmonitoring and auditing suppliers, and the impact of these activities on the overall quality of\\ndata security management. Finally, an interesting direction of research would be to examine the\\neffectiveness of integrating technologies and organizational strategies in the context of data\\nsecurity.  Analyzing  the  synergies  between  technologies  and  security  policies  could  provide\\nknowledge on the most effective combinations of actions that provide holistic data protection\\nin a dynamically changing business environment. Introduction\\n\\nThe issue of customer data security in agile organizations is becoming crucial in the context\\nof contemporary challenges posed by digital transformation and dynamically changing market\\nconditions  (Awasthi,  Awasthi,  2023).  The  ongoing  digitalization  of  business  processes,\\nthe growing importance of data as a strategic resource, and the growing number of cyber threats\\nmake data protection not only an operational priority, but also the foundation for building trust\\nand long-term relationships with customers. The conducted research focused on the analysis of\\nfactors  determining  customer  data  security  in  agile  organizations  allows  for  a  better\\nunderstanding of which  management elements in this area are key  and what challenges  are\\nassociated with their implementation (Kurnia, Chien, 2020).\\nThe  article  begins  with  a  theoretical  introduction  that  focuses  on  the  importance  of\\nprotecting customer data in the context of organizational agility. Then, the research objective\\nis  presented,  which  is  to  identify  and  assess  key  factors  for  ensuring  data  security  in  agile\\norganizations. The research methodology used is also described, including the use of a survey\\nconducted on a sample of 303 respondents and multivariate correspondence analysis (MCA),\\nwhich  allows  for  the  identification  of  patterns  in  the  respondents’  answers.  The  subsequent\\nsections of the article present detailed research results, including the respondents’ assessments\\nof  individual  factors  and  the  analysis  of  the  relationships  between  them. The Importance of Keeping Customer Data Secure\\n\\nEnsuring  the  security  of  customer  data  is  a  key  element  of  the  functioning  of  modern\\norganizations, especially in the era of dynamic development of digital technologies and the\\ngrowing importance of data as a strategic resource. Customer data, both personal and business,\\nare one of the most valuable assets of every organization, which is why their protection is not\\nonly a legal requirement, but also a fundamental aspect of building trust and reputation (Jones,\\nAdam, 2023).\\n\\n## [PDF page 177]\\n\\nFactors determining customer data security…  177\\n\\nCustomer data security directly affects the perception of an organization as professional,\\nresponsible, and trustworthy. As customers become more aware of the risks associated with\\nprivacy  breaches,  expectations  of  organizations  regarding  data  protection  are  growing\\nsignificantly. Data loss or improper protection can lead to serious consequences, such as loss\\nof  trust,  decreased  customer  loyalty,  and  a  negative  impact  on  the  organization’s  financial\\nresults. Moreover, in an era of increasingly stringent legal regulations, such as GDPR in the\\nEuropean Union, improper management of customer data can result in severe financial and\\nlegal penalties (LexDigital, 2022).\\nFrom the perspective of agile organizations, which are flexible and able to quickly adapt to\\nchanging market conditions, ensuring the security of customer data is particularly important.\\nSuch  organizations  often  operate  in  a  highly  digitalized  environment  and  use  advanced\\ntechnological  tools  to  manage  processes  and  communicate  with  customers  (EITT,  2024).\\nAs a result, their activities are exposed to various threats, such as hacker attacks, data leaks or\\nunauthorized access to systems (Chen, Siau, 2020). Ensuring data security requires a systemic\\nand multi-faceted approach. A key element is the use of advanced technologies, such as data\\nencryption, access control, regular security audits or real-time monitoring. At the same time,\\neducation of employees plays an important role, who must be aware of the threats and properly\\ntrained  in  data  protection.  Implementing  procedures  for  handling  security  incidents  helps\\nminimize the potential effects of breaches (LexDigital, 2022).\\nCustomer  data  security  also  has  an  important  ethical  dimension.  Organizations  are\\nresponsible for protecting the information entrusted to them, and any failure to do so can be\\nperceived as a lack of respect for customers and their privacy (Joiner, 2019). Therefore, building\\nan organizational culture in which data protection is a priority plays a key role in long-term\\nbusiness  success  (ODO24,  2024).  In  the  context  of  contemporary  challenges  such  as\\nglobalization, the development of cloud computing, or the growing number of cyberattacks,\\nensuring  the  security  of  customer  data  is  not  a  one-time  action,  but  a  process  that  requires\\ncontinuous optimization and adaptation to new threats. Organizations that effectively integrate\\ndata security management with daily operations not only gain a competitive advantage, but also\\nbuild lasting relationships with customers based on trust and loyalty (Luo, Ren, Cao, Hong,\\n2020).\\n\\n1.2.  Customer Perception in Agile Organizations\\n\\nThe customer in agile organizations is a key element of the strategy of action, because it is\\nthe customer who is the center of all processes and decisions (Raschke, 2010; Womack, Jones,\\n2003; Yang, Liu, 2012). In the context of organizational agility, the customer is not perceived\\nonly as a recipient of a product or service, but as an active participant whose needs, expectations\\nand  opinions  significantly  shape  the  functioning  of  the  organization.  This  way  of  thinking\\nresults  from  the  philosophy  of  agility,  which  assumes  dynamic  adaptation  to  the  changing\\nenvironment  and  continuous  improvement  of  the  offer  (Gadomska-Lila,  2013). Thanks to this, organizations can respond\\nto changing trends, identify new market opportunities, and anticipate future customer needs.\\nInstead of relying on outdated patterns of action, agile organizations dynamically adapt to the\\nenvironment, which allows them to remain competitive. Another important aspect of customer\\nperception in agile organizations is personalization (Doz, Kosonen, 2008). Agile organizations\\nstrive to provide individually tailored solutions that take into account the specific preferences\\nand expectations of each customer. Personalization not only  increases customer\\nsatisfaction, but also strengthens their loyalty to the brand (Gao, Zhang, Gong, Li, 2020).\\nThe  customer  in  agile  organizations  is  also  seen  as  a  partner  in  the  process  of  building\\norganizational value. The agile approach assumes that the relationship with the customer does\\nnot end at the sales stage, but lasts throughout the entire life cycle of the product or service.\\nRegular interactions and collecting feedback allow organizations to continuously improve the\\noffer  and  increase  the  value  delivered  to  customers.  However,  such  an  approach  requires\\nopenness to dialogue and flexibility in responding to criticism and changing needs (Rahimi,\\nMansouri, 2019). Their results allow\\nfor making informed decisions regarding further investments in security and minimizing the\\nrisk of breaches (Sedej, Justinek, 2021).\\nAn essential element of the security strategy in agile organizations is employee education\\nin the field of data protection. In  the  context  of\\norganizational agility, where teams work in a dynamic environment, this education must be\\na permanent element of the company’s policy (Routledge, 2020). Employee knowledge is a key\\nfactor in data protection, because even the most advanced technologies can be ineffective in the\\nface of human  errors (Thales, 2022). Implementing  monitoring  systems\\nallows not only the identification of potential breaches, but also rapid response to incidents,\\nwhich minimizes the risk of problem escalation (Seifollahi, Shirazian, 2021).\\n\\n## [PDF page 180]\\n\\n180  M. Discussion\\n\\nThe research results allowed us to draw several important conclusions regarding the factors\\ndetermining the security of customer data in agile organizations. These audits,\\nbeing  part  of  prevention  and  monitoring,  are  seen  as  essential  in  the  process  of  continuous\\nimprovement of security systems. The results emphasize the need for their cyclical conduct to\\nensure compliance with dynamically changing standards and technological requirements.\\n\\n## [PDF page 184]\\n\\n184  M. Kocot, B. Today’s agile organizations increasingly use analytical tools that enable ongoing control\\nand  response  to  security  incidents  (ODO24,  2024).  Regular  updates  of  software  and\\ntechnological infrastructure are equally important. Lack of updates can lead to the exploitation\\nof known vulnerabilities in systems, which significantly increases the risk of security breaches\\n(LexDigital, 2022).\\nDeveloping and implementing procedures for handling data breaches is another important\\nelement  of  the  security  strategy.  The  literature  emphasizes  that  appropriate  incident\\nmanagement and rapid response to breaches are crucial to minimizing the effects of such events\\n(BCO-Integrity, 2024). Interdisciplinary cooperation in security management has been assessed\\nas an important factor, which is confirmed by research by other authors. Combining knowledge\\nand  experience  from  different  areas,  such  as  IT,  law  or  management,  leads  to  more\\ncomprehensive and effective solutions (EITT, 2024).\\nIn summary, the research results and their comparison with the literature on the subject\\nindicate the need for a comprehensive approach to managing customer data security. Technical\\naspects,  such  as  encryption  and  monitoring,  must  be  supplemented  with  organizational\\nactivities, including staff education and interdisciplinary cooperation, to effectively protect data\\nin a dynamically changing organizational environment.\\nThe  limitations  of  the  research  stem  from  several  key  aspects  that  may  affect  the\\ninterpretation of the results and their generalization. First, the study was conducted exclusively\\nin the context of agile organizations, which may limit the applicability of the conclusions to\\n\\n## [PDF page 187]\\n\\nFactors determining customer data security…  187\\n\\nother types of enterprises, such as hierarchical or traditional organizations. The results reflect\\nthe  specificity  of  agile  work  environments,  which  are  characterized  by  high  dynamics  and\\nflexibility, which may differ from structures less susceptible to rapid changes.\\nAnother limitation is the data collection method. A survey based on subjective opinions of\\nrespondents may lead to errors resulting from the interpretation of questions, the diversity of\\nprofessional experiences of participants, or their individual preferences. Although the sample\\nsize of 303 people provides a solid basis for analysis, the results may be partially limited by the\\nlack of full representativeness of different industries and sectors. In addition, the multivariate\\ncorrespondence  analysis  (MCA)  method  used,  although  extremely  useful  in  discovering\\nrelationships between variables, has its limitations. The results are sensitive to the quality of\\nthe input data and may  not fully reflect more complex relationships between the categories\\nstudied. MCA analysis allows for the identification of patterns and relationships, but does not\\nprovide direct information about causality or the direction of these relationships.\\nThe time context of the study may also have an impact on its limitations. The study was\\nconducted in April–May 2023, which means that the results reflect the specific technological\\nand social conditions of that period. The rapid development of technology and changing legal\\nregulations  may  mean  that  some  conclusions  require  regular  updates  to  remain  relevant  in\\na  dynamically  changing  organizational  environment.  Another  limitation may  be  the  lack  of\\nconsideration for the perspective of customers whose data is subject to protection. The study\\nfocused on the perception of representatives of organizations, which may not fully reflect the\\nexpectations  and  needs  of  customers  themselves  in  terms  of  the  security  of  their  data.\\nThese aspects indicate the need for continued research that could include more diverse groups\\nof respondents and additional methods of analysis.\\nFuture  research  directions  could  focus  on  extending  the  analysis  to  other  types  of\\norganizations, such as hierarchical or traditional structures, to see to what extent the factors\\ndetermining data security differ depending on the specific organizational setting. An important\\narea for further research is also comparative analysis between different industries, which would\\nallow to determine which sectors are more exposed to threats related to data protection and\\nwhich strategies are most effective in their context. Research  could  also  include  an  analysis  of  the  interactions  between\\ntechnological, organizational and cultural factors in ensuring data security, which would allow\\nfor  a  fuller  understanding  of  their  mutual  dependencies  and  impact  on  the  effectiveness  of\\ninformation protection.\\nAnother  research  area  could  be  the  evaluation  of  the  effectiveness  of  implementing\\nindividual  recommendations  resulting  from  the  current  study. Introduction\\n\\nIT outsourcing plays an increasingly important role in the management strategies of modern\\norganizations,  offering  access  to  advanced  technologies  and  specialized  resources  that  are\\ndifficult to develop internally. However, the success of such collaboration largely depends on\\nthe  quality  of  communication  between  the  organization  and  external  providers.  Effective\\ncommunication  is  essential  for  precisely  defining  expectations,  minimizing  the  risk  of\\nmisunderstandings,  and  efficiently  responding  to  changing  conditions  of  cooperation.\\nThe complexity of outsourcing processes necessitates adequate  communication support that\\nfosters the development of sustainable and effective partnerships (Zhen, Xie, Dong, 2021).\\nThe purpose of this study is to investigate actions supporting effective communication in\\nIT outsourcing processes and to identify those perceived as the most effective. The following\\nresearch  hypotheses  are  proposed:  (1)  Standardizing  communication  processes  significantly\\nenhances the effectiveness of outsourcing collaboration; (2) The use of modern technologies\\nsupports  the  fluidity  and  precision  of  information  exchange;  (3)  Building  a  culture  of  trust\\npositively  affects  the  quality  of  outsourcing  relationships;  (4)  Flexible  responses  to\\ncommunication challenges minimize the risk of disruptions in project implementation.\\nThe  research  methodology  included  an  analysis  of  responses  from  723  participants,\\ncollected  via  a  survey,  and  the  application  of  multiple  correspondence  analysis  (MCA),\\nwhich enabled the identification of patterns in the perception of specific  actions supporting\\ncommunication.  The  introduction  of  these  analytical  techniques  yielded  innovative  results,\\nhighlighting key factors that determine communication success in IT outsourcing.\\nThe  current  state  of  research  indicates  that  the  effectiveness  of  communication  in\\nIT  outsourcing  depends  on  the  integration  of  several  interrelated  factors.  Key  publications\\n(Felipe, Leander, Roldan, Leal-Rodriguez, 2020; Zhen, Xie, Dong, 2021) emphasize the role\\nof  technology,  standardization  processes,  and  trust  in  shaping  outsourcing  relationships.\\nThis paper builds upon these findings, providing practical recommendations for organizations.\\nThe added value of this article lies in combining theoretical perspectives with empirical\\nresearch findings, allowing for a comprehensive  understanding of the problem and offering\\npractical insights. The results can be particularly useful for managers and specialists involved\\nin  managing  outsourcing  relationships,  offering  concrete  guidance  on  actions  that  enhance\\ncommunication effectiveness.\\n\\n## [PDF page 195]\\n\\nActivities supporting communication efficiency…  195\\n\\n2.  Literature review\\n\\n2.1.  The essence of IT outsourcing\\n\\nThe essence of IT outsourcing is to transfer part or all of an organization’s IT functions to\\nan  external  service  provider  in  order  to  achieve  operational,  strategic  or  financial  benefits.\\nIT outsourcing has become an important management tool in many organizations that want to\\nfocus on their core competencies while using specialized external resources. This allows access\\nto modern technologies, expert knowledge and advanced IT solutions that would be difficult or\\nexpensive to achieve internally (Chakrabarty, 2006).\\nIT  outsourcing  covers  a  wide  range  of  services,  such  as  IT  infrastructure  management,\\nsoftware development and maintenance, cybersecurity, cloud storage, and technical support.\\nOrganizations often decide on such solutions to reduce the costs associated with hiring and\\ntraining IT staff, purchasing equipment, and maintaining internal IT systems. Outsourcing also\\nallows them to flexibly adapt IT resources to changing needs, which is especially important in\\na dynamic business environment (Lacity, Willcocks, 2013).\\nThe key element of IT outsourcing is cooperation between the organization and the service\\nprovider,  which  requires  effective  communication,  clearly  defined  goals,  and  appropriately\\nformulated agreements. This process involves the need to precisely define the scope of tasks,\\nexpected results, and quality standards (Kłos, 2009). Outsourcing agreements, such as SLA\\n(Service Level Agreement), are the basis of the relationship between the parties and ensure that\\nthe service provider meets the customer\'s requirements (Raišienė, Bilan, Smalskys, Gečienė,\\n2019).\\nIT outsourcing allows organizations not only to reduce costs, but also to increase innovation\\nand improve efficiency. Service providers often have advanced technologies and experts who\\ncan  introduce  new  solutions,  support  digital  transformation,  and  contribute  to  achieving\\nstrategic goals. Outsourcing can also reduce technology risk, as service providers have greater\\nability to manage updates, compliance with regulations, and data protection (Krull, Mackinnon,\\n2016).\\nHowever,  IT outsourcing also involves certain challenges and risks. Organizations must\\nconsider potential problems such as loss of control over key processes, dependence on external\\nsuppliers,  data  protection  risks,  and  conflicts  resulting  from  cultural  and  time  differences.\\nEffective outsourcing management therefore requires appropriate control mechanisms, constant\\nmonitoring of service quality, and building long-term, trust-based relationships with suppliers\\n(Porter Heppelmann, 2014).\\n\\n## [PDF page 196]\\n\\n196  D. Kocot, K. Olejko\\n\\nIn  summary,  IT  outsourcing  is  a  complex  process  that  can  bring  significant  benefits  to\\norganizations if managed properly. Its essence is to use external resources to achieve higher\\nefficiency, flexibility, and competitiveness in a rapidly changing technological and business\\nenvironment.\\n\\n2.2.  The role of effective communication in an organization\\n\\nEffective communication plays a key role in the functioning of any organization, as it is the\\nfoundation on which cooperation, decision-making and the implementation of strategic goals\\nare  based  (Quelin,  Duhamel,  2003).  Without  an  efficient  flow  of  information  between\\nindividuals, teams or departments, the organization is exposed to misunderstandings, delays in\\ntask implementation and a decrease in efficiency. Communication in an organization is not only\\nan  operational  tool,  but  also  an  element  of  building  an  organizational  culture  that  affects\\nemployee motivation, commitment and satisfaction (Dhillon, Backhouse, 2001).\\nEffective  communication supports the exchange of knowledge and experience, which is\\nparticularly important in a dynamic business environment, where innovation and adaptability\\nbecome key success factors (Lacity, Willcocks, 2009). Organizations that are able to ensure\\ntransparency of information and openness in dialogue gain a competitive advantage because\\nthey  respond  faster  to  changing  market  conditions  and  implement  new  solutions  more\\neffectively (Cullen, Seddon, Willcocks, 2005).  Transparent communication also helps build\\ntrust in both internal and external relationships, which is important in the context of cooperation\\nwith  business  partners,  customers,  and  suppliers  (Kern,  Willcocks,  Van  Heck,  2013).\\nIn  an  organization,  communication  also  plays  a  role  in  supporting  the  change  management\\nprocess.  In  transformation  situations,  such  as  restructuring,  introducing  new  technologies,\\nor  changes  in  the  organizational  structure,  effective  information  transfer  helps  minimize\\nemployee  resistance  and  increase  their  acceptance  of  the  changes  being  introduced.\\nClear and consistent messages help explain the reasons for decisions, present expected benefits,\\nand define new roles and responsibilities, which reduces uncertainty and tensions within the\\nteam (Qureshi, 2016).\\nAn important aspect of effective communication is its impact on decision-making processes\\n(Lacity, Willcocks, 2010). Quick and precise access to information allows leaders to make good\\ndecisions based on reliable data. At the same time, openness to diverse perspectives resulting\\nfrom dialogue with employees allows for taking into account various aspects of problems and\\napproaching  them  in  a  more  comprehensive  way.  In  turn,  in  relations  between  employees,\\ncommunication helps clarify doubts, resolve conflicts and create an atmosphere of cooperation\\n(Gupta,  Puranam,  Srikanth,  2006),  which  affects  better  team  integration  (Pandita,  Singhal,\\n2017).\\n\\n## [PDF page 197]\\n\\nActivities supporting communication efficiency…  197\\n\\nEffective  communication  also  contributes  to  strengthening  employee  engagement  by\\nbuilding  a  sense  of  belonging  to  the  organization.  Employees  who  are  informed  about  the\\ncompany’s  goals,  values,  and  strategy  better  understand  their  roles  and  their  importance  in\\nachieving the organization’s mission. Communication based on openness and dialogue  also\\npromotes  identification  with  the  organization,  which  translates  into  higher  loyalty  and\\nwillingness to take additional actions for the company (Kane, Palmer, Nguyen Phillips, Kiron,\\nBuckley, 2015).\\nEffective  communication,  however,  requires  the  right  tools,  technologies  and  skills.\\nOrganizations must invest in the development of employee communication skills and provide\\nplatforms that allow for quick and easy access to information. It is also crucial to adapt the\\ncommunication  style  to  the  needs  and  preferences  of  different  groups  of  recipients,  which\\nallows  for  increasing  its  effectiveness.  In  the  era  of  digital  transformation,  effective\\ncommunication  is  becoming  an  increasingly  strategic  element  of  management,  which\\ndetermines the success of an organization in an increasingly competitive market.\\n\\n2.3.  IT outsourcing and ensuring effective communication in the organization\\n\\nIT outsourcing poses numerous challenges for organizations related to ensuring effective\\ncommunication,  which  is  the  foundation  of  successful  cooperation  with  external  suppliers.\\nThis  process  requires  not  only  the  implementation  of  appropriate  mechanisms  and  tools,\\nbut  also  the  development  of  standards  that  will  allow  for  the  consistency  and  clarity  of\\ninformation  exchange  between  the  parties  (Kern,  Willcocks,  Van  Heck,  2015).  Effective\\ncommunication  in  this  context  includes  both  precise  definition  of  expectations  and  goals,\\nas well as ongoing exchange of information during project implementation, which allows for\\na  faster  response  to  emerging  challenges  (Constantinides,  2014).  One  of  the  key  elements\\nsupporting  communication  in  IT  outsourcing  is  the  implementation  of  communication\\nstandards that regulate the method, frequency and form of information transfer. Standardization\\nof  these  processes  allows  for  the  elimination  of  potential  misunderstandings  and  improves\\ncooperation between internal teams and external suppliers. The introduction of such standards\\nallows for the organization of the communication process, which increases the transparency of\\nactivities and facilitates monitoring of progress in project implementation (Yin et al., 2020).\\nThe  second  important  factor  supporting  the  effectiveness  of  communication  in\\nIT outsourcing is the use of modern technologies that enable the smooth flow of information.\\nTools  such  as  project  management  systems,  online  collaboration  platforms  or  data  analysis\\napplications allow for the ongoing exchange of information in a fast, precise and accessible\\nmanner  for  all  stakeholders  (Danneels,  Kleinschmidt,  2016).  Technology  also  supports  the\\nautomation of certain aspects of communication, which minimizes the risk of errors resulting\\nfrom the human factor and increases the efficiency of the entire process. Another important\\naspect  in  the  context  of  communication  is  building  a  culture  of  trust  and  transparency  in\\n\\n## [PDF page 198]\\n\\n198  D. Kocot, K. Olejko\\n\\noutsourcing  relationships  (Galvin,  2019).  Trust  between  the  parties  is  the  foundation  of\\nsuccessful cooperation and allows for the open expression of needs, concerns and suggestions\\nregarding  implemented  projects.  Transparency  of  activities,  including  regular  progress\\nreporting,  clearly  defined  expectations  and  openness  to  dialogue,  favors  building  lasting\\npartnerships  that  are  less  susceptible  to  conflicts  and  misunderstandings  (Turban,  Outland,\\nKing, Lee, Liang, Turban, 2018).\\nEffective communication in IT outsourcing also requires the ability to respond quickly to\\nemerging challenges and problems. Flexibility in adapting to changing conditions or unforeseen\\ncircumstances allows for minimizing losses and ensuring business continuity. Organizations\\nthat are able to quickly adapt their communication processes to crisis situations are able to better\\nmanage risk and maintain a high level of efficiency (Uhl-Bien, Arena, 2017).\\nEnsuring effective communication in IT outsourcing is not limited to tools and procedures,\\nbut  also  includes  developing  soft  skills  among  employees  responsible  for  cooperation  with\\nsuppliers. Skills such as active listening, negotiation skills or clear formulation of thoughts are\\nkey  to  building  positive  relationships  and  increasing  the  effectiveness  of  communication.\\nEmployees  equipped  with  the  right  skills  are  able  to  manage  relationships  better,  which\\ntranslates into greater trust and commitment of both parties (Ravichandran, 2016).\\nIn summary, effective communication in IT outsourcing is a complex process that requires\\nthe integration of many elements, such as process standardization, use of technology, building\\na culture of trust, and the ability to flexibly respond to changing conditions. These activities are\\nkey to the success of outsourcing projects and allow for the creation of stable and effective\\nrelationships between organizations and suppliers.\\n\\n3.  Methods\\n\\nThe aim of the conducted research was to identify actions supporting the effectiveness of\\ncommunication in IT outsourcing and to analyze their perception by respondents in the context\\nof  key  aspects  of  outsourcing  cooperation.  It  was  assumed  that  effective  communication\\nbetween internal teams and IT service providers, supported by specific actions, significantly\\naffects the quality of cooperation and achievement of business goals. The research hypothesis\\nindicated  that  specific  actions,  such  as  implementing  communication  standards,  using  new\\ntechnologies or building a culture of trust, differ in terms of their perceived effectiveness by the\\nresearch participants.\\nThe research method was a survey  conducted in 2023 on  a sample of 723 respondents.\\nThe survey allowed for  collecting data on the perception of individual activities supporting\\ncommunication in IT outsourcing. Discussion\\n\\nThe research shows that the effectiveness of communication in IT outsourcing is strongly\\ndependent  on  the  implementation  of  activities  supporting  cooperation  between  the  internal\\nteams of the organization and external suppliers. Communication standards play a key role,\\nensuring consistency and transparency in the transfer of information, which reduces the risk of\\nmisunderstandings and delays in project implementation. It has been shown that activities based\\non building a culture of trust and transparency are of particular importance for strengthening\\n\\n## [PDF page 202]\\n\\n202  D. Kocot, K. Olejko\\n\\nrelations  between  the  parties,  which  translates  into  greater  efficiency  and  stability  of\\ncooperation.  Technologies  supporting  the  smooth  flow  of  information  were  assessed  as\\nan important element in the process of improving communication. The use of appropriate digital\\ntools allows for more effective task management, quick access to necessary information and\\neasier tracking of  work  progress. The  research highlighted the importance of responding to\\ncommunication challenges in real time, which emphasizes the need for flexibility and the ability\\nto quickly adapt to changing conditions.\\nMultivariate correspondence analysis revealed patterns in the perception of communication\\nsupport activities, which indicates differences in the priorities and expectations of individual\\ngroups  of  respondents.  Identification  of  these  patterns  allows  for  matching  communication\\nstrategies to the specific needs of organizations and suppliers. The results  of the study also\\nemphasize that the effectiveness of communication in IT outsourcing is not only the result of\\napplying individual activities, but requires a coherent approach encompassing many mutually\\ncomplementary elements.\\nResearch shows that the lack of effective communication mechanisms can lead to problems\\nin  project  implementation,  reduced  efficiency  and  decreased  trust  between  partners.\\nConsequently,  implementing  communication  support  activities  allows  not  only  to  improve\\nrelationships,  but  also  to  increase  the  satisfaction  and  commitment  of  outsourcing  process\\nparticipants. The obtained results can be the basis for developing practical recommendations\\nthat will help organizations better manage outsourcing relationships and maximize the benefits\\nresulting from this form of cooperation.\\nBased on the results obtained, it is recommended that companies take action to strengthen\\ncommunication standards in outsourcing processes. The introduction of consistent procedures\\nand clear rules for the exchange of information between internal teams and external suppliers\\nis crucial. Standardization of communication will help avoid misunderstandings and increase\\nthe  efficiency  of  project  implementation.  It  is  also  important  to  use  modern  technologies\\nsupporting the flow of information, which enable ongoing access to data, monitoring of work\\nprogress and quick response to emerging problems. Selecting the right digital tools, such as\\nproject management systems or communication platforms, can significantly improve the quality\\nof cooperation.\\nIt is recommended to invest in building a culture of trust and transparency in outsourcing\\nrelationships.  Regular  communication  based  on  openness  and  clear  definition  of  goals  and\\nexpectations allows for reducing tensions and strengthening partnerships. Striving for greater\\ntransparency in the activities of both parties has a positive impact on the quality of cooperation\\nand the level of commitment.\\nCompanies  should  also  ensure  flexibility  in  responding  to  communication  challenges.\\nQuick identification of problems and their ongoing resolution allows for minimizing disruptions\\nin  project  implementation  and  building  positive  experiences  for  both  the  customer  and  the\\n\\n## [PDF page 203]\\n\\nActivities supporting communication efficiency…  203\\n\\nsupplier. Creating dedicated teams responsible for monitoring communication and providing\\nsupport in crisis situations can contribute to greater efficiency of operations.\\nThe need to adapt communication strategies to the specific needs of different outsourcing\\npartners  is  also  emphasized.  Analysis  of  patterns  of  perception  of  activities  by  process\\nparticipants allows for better adjustment of tools and methods of cooperation, which increases\\nthe effectiveness of undertaken activities. Companies can introduce training programs aimed at\\nimproving  communication  skills  of  employees,  which  will  affect  better  understanding  of\\nexpectations and challenges of both parties.\\n\\n6.  Conclusions\\n\\nThe results of the conducted research on actions supporting communication effectiveness\\nin IT outsourcing are consistent with the findings of other researchers in this field. In particular,\\nthe  emphasis  on  the  importance  of  implementing  communication  standards  and  building\\na culture of trust and transparency is reflected in the literature on the subject.\\nResearch conducted by Annarelli, Colabianchi, Nonino, and Palombi (2021) indicates that\\nthe effectiveness of cybersecurity outsourcing practices is strongly related to the management\\nof  relationships  between  organizations  and  service  providers.  The  authors  emphasize  that\\ndifferences in the effectiveness of cybersecurity management are due to whether these processes\\nare managed internally or outsourced, suggesting that communication standards and a culture\\nof trust play a key role in the success of outsourcing.\\nSimilarly,  Murphy  (2024)  in  his  study  analyzes  the  impact  of  IT  outsourcing  on\\norganizational  success  and  innovation.  The  results  indicate  that  effective  communication\\nbetween internal teams and external suppliers is crucial to achieving positive results. The author\\nemphasizes  that  the  lack  of  appropriate  communication  mechanisms  can  lead  to  failures  in\\noutsourcing  projects.  Additionally,  research  conducted  by  Ali  and  Green  (2009)  on\\nIT governance mechanisms indicates that the effectiveness of IT governance in an organization\\nhas a direct impact on IT outsourcing decisions. The authors emphasize that organizations with\\neffective IT governance are better prepared to make outsourcing decisions, which suggests that\\ncommunication standards and a culture of trust are crucial for the success of such initiatives.\\nIn summary, the results of this study are consistent with the findings of other researchers,\\nemphasizing the importance of communication standards, a culture of trust, and transparency\\nin the effective management of IT outsourcing processes. Olejko\\n\\nThe limitations of research based on the analysis of actions supporting the effectiveness of\\ncommunication in IT outsourcing result primarily from the methodological approach used and\\nthe specificity of the research sample. One of the main limitations is basing the analysis on data\\ncollected exclusively by means of a survey. Although this method allows for the collection of\\na large amount of information in a short time, the results may be susceptible to the subjective\\nnature  of  respondents’  answers.  This  may  affect  the  accuracy  of  the  assessment  of  actions\\nsupporting communication and limit the possibility of their generalization to other groups.\\nAn  additional  limitation  is  the  fact  that  the  survey  was  conducted  on  a  sample  of  723\\nrespondents,  which,  although  it  provides  a  broad  picture  of  opinions,  may  not  be  fully\\nrepresentative of all sectors and types of IT outsourcing. The characteristics of the respondents,\\nsuch as their professional experience, role in the organization or industry specificity, may affect\\nthe perception of the surveyed activities. This limits the possibility of applying the results to\\nsectors significantly different from the surveyed group.\\nMCA analysis, although it provides valuable information about the relationships between\\nvariables, is based on reducing data to dimensions, which is associated with the loss of some\\ndetailed information. In addition, the interpretation of MCA results requires the adoption of\\ncertain assumptions that can affect the final conclusions. In particular, the choice of the number\\nof  dimensions  used  in  the  analysis  can  limit  the  full  reflection  of  the  complexity  of  the\\nrelationships between variables.\\nAnother limitation is the lack of consideration of the cultural and organizational context,\\nwhich can significantly affect the perception of communication effectiveness in IT outsourcing.\\nDifferences in management practices and expectations towards IT service providers may mean\\nthat these results will not be fully translatable to other countries or organizations with different\\norganizational cultures.\\nThe  results  could  also  be  influenced  by  changes  in  the  dynamically  developing\\ntechnological environment. Introduction\\n\\nModern  organizations  operate  in  a  dynamically  changing  economic  environment  that\\nrequires flexibility, innovation, and the ability to respond quickly to emerging challenges (Nath,\\nAgrawal,  2020).  In  this  context,  building  an  employer  image  is  becoming  increasingly\\nimportant, which allows attracting and retaining talented employees, who are a key resource in\\nagile organizations. The image of an attractive employer is no longer just an element of the\\nhuman  resources  management  strategy,  becoming  an  important  factor  influencing  the\\ncompetitiveness  and  adaptability  of  the  organization.  In  agile  organizational  structures,\\nwhere flexibility and teamwork efficiency are of fundamental importance, motivational factors\\nthat respond to the diverse needs of employees are of particular importance (Prieto, Talukder,\\n2023).\\nTaking  up  this  topic  is  justified  by  the  growing  importance  of  employer  branding  as\\na strategic tool that affects not only the acquisition of new talents, but also the engagement and\\nloyalty of current employees. In the environment of agile organizations, where the culture of\\nopenness  and  innovation  plays  a  key  role,  understanding  the  determinants  that  build  the\\nemployer’s image becomes a necessity. Proper identification and analysis of these factors allows\\norganizations to respond more effectively to employee expectations, which translates into their\\nsatisfaction and work efficiency. The importance of this issue also results from the growing\\ncompetition on the labor market and the need to build lasting relationships with employees in\\norganizations operating in the agile model.\\nThe aim of the article is to analyze the key motivational factors that influence the creation\\nof the employer image in agile organizations. The research attempted to identify the elements\\nthat are most important from the perspective of employees and to determine their significance\\nin the process of shaping employer branding. The article combines theoretical and empirical\\napproaches,  which  allows  for  a  more  comprehensive  picture  of  the  issue  under  study.\\nThe  structure  of  the  study  includes  a  theoretical  part,  which  provides  a  foundation  for  the\\nanalysis of motivational factors,  and a  research part, which presents the  results of a survey\\nconducted  on  a  sample  of  303  respondents.  The  research  used  multidimensional\\ncorrespondence analysis (MCA), which enabled the identification of relationships between the\\nvariables studied and the preferences of respondents.\\nThe added value of the article is an in-depth analysis of the importance of motivational\\nfactors  in  the  context  of  employer  branding  from  the  perspective  of  agile  organizations.\\nThe research results can be the basis for developing practical recommendations for managers\\nand  leaders  of  organizations  who  strive  to  strengthen  their  image  as  attractive  employers.\\nThe  use  of  multidimensional  analysis  allows  for  obtaining  unique  observations  regarding\\nresponse patterns, which can be used as a tool for more effective human resources management.\\nThe article fits into the trend of research on the sustainable development of an organization and\\n\\n## [PDF page 211]\\n\\nMotivational factors building the image…  211\\n\\nits  ability  to  adapt  to  a  changing  environment,  while  providing  practical  tips  for  modern\\norganizations.\\n\\n1.1.  The Role of Employer Image in an Agile Organization\\n\\nThe  role  of  employer  image  in  an  agile  organization  plays  a  key  role  in  building  its\\ncompetitiveness and ability to attract and retain talented employees (Mrugalska, Ahmed, 2021).\\nIn a dynamically changing business environment, agile organizations focus on flexibility, quick\\nresponse  to  change,  and  innovation,  which  requires  a  committed  and  motivated  team.\\nAn  employer  image  that  is  perceived  as  attractive  and  trustworthy  becomes  an  important\\nelement  of  the  human  resources  management  strategy  and  affects  the  effectiveness  of  the\\norganization (Sedej, Justinek, 2021).\\nIn agile organizations, the ability to create a work environment that meets the expectations\\nof modern employees plays a special role. The employer’s image is based not only on material\\naspects, such as remuneration and benefits, but also on intangible values, such as organizational\\nculture,  professional  development  opportunities  or  care  for  work-life  balance  (Lane,  2016).\\nBuilding the image of the organization as an employer who promotes openness, cooperation\\nand  flexibility  affects  the  perception  of  the  company  as  modern  and  employee-friendly.\\nAgile organizations that effectively shape their image gain an advantage in acquiring the best\\ntalents on the labor market (Seifollahi, Shirazian, 2021).\\nOrganizational culture plays a particularly important role in this context, because in agile\\norganizations, the emphasis is on teamwork, transparent communication, and quick decision-\\nmaking (Kusibab, 2013). Employees expect that their opinions will be heard and that their work\\nwill have a real impact on the development of the organization. Transparency in management,\\nmutual respect, and promoting innovation build trust in the employer, which in turn strengthens\\nits  positive  image.  Agile  organizations  that  invest  in  a  culture  based  on  values  create\\nan environment that promotes employee engagement and loyalty (Zając-Pałdyna, 2020).\\nFlexibility  is  one  of  the  foundations  of  the  employer  image  in  an  agile  organization.\\nThe ability to adjust working hours, perform duties remotely or implement modern cooperation\\nmodels  are  aspects  that  are  particularly  appreciated  by  employees.  This  flexibility  allows\\nemployees to manage their time more effectively and achieve a work-life balance, which affects\\ntheir satisfaction and motivation to work. An organization that offers flexible forms of work is\\nperceived as more modern, responsible and aware of the needs of its employees (Rzewuska\\net al., 2013).\\nThe use of modern technologies is another element of building the employer’s image in\\nan agile organization (Näppä, 2023). Tools supporting communication, project management\\nand process automation are not only an expression of innovation, but also facilitate the work of\\nteams and improve the efficiency of the organization. An employer who implements modern\\ntechnological solutions gains a reputation of an organization that cares about the development\\nand comfort of its employees. Access to modern tools is also an important factor in attracting\\n\\n## [PDF page 212]\\n\\n212  M. Kocot, K. Olejko\\n\\nyounger generations of employees, for whom innovation and digitization are key aspects of the\\nwork environment (|ółkiewicz, Olszewski, Czarnecki, 2021).\\nTaking  care  of  employees’  professional  development  is  an  integral  part  of  a  positive\\nemployer  image  in  an  agile  organization  (Kozłowski,  2016).  The  introduction  of  training\\nprograms, mentoring, or promotion opportunities is particularly important in an environment\\ncharacterized  by  a  high  pace  of  change  and  a  constant  pursuit  of  improvement.  Employees\\nperceive an organization as an attractive employer if they can develop their competences and\\nfulfill their professional ambitions there. Investing in team development is not only an element\\nthat  builds  employee  loyalty,  but  also  contributes  to  the  increase  in  the  efficiency  of  the\\norganization as a whole (Zak, 2022).\\nThe role of employer image in an agile organization is also related to the ability to respond\\nquickly  to  employee  needs.  Organizations  that  dynamically  adapt  to  changing  team\\nexpectations  build  their  reputation  as  an  employer  that  cares  about  the  well-being  and\\nsatisfaction  of  staff.  This  type  of  approach  strengthens  relationships  with  employees  and\\ncontributes  to  an  increase  in  the  level  of  commitment  and  loyalty  to  the  organization\\n(Szkudlarek, 2022).\\nIn summary, the employer image of an agile organization is a key factor in its ability to\\nattract  and  retain  talent.  Building  this  image  is  based  on  promoting  flexibility,  innovation,\\nopenness,  and  concern  for  the  development  and  needs  of  employees.  Organizations  that\\neffectively  shape  their  image  not  only  gain  an  advantage  in  the  competitive  labor  market,\\nbut also create an environment that promotes team engagement, loyalty, and effectiveness.\\n\\n1.2.  Motivational factors in an agile organization and their importance\\n\\nMotivational factors in an agile organization play an important role in shaping employee\\nengagement,  job  satisfaction,  and  team  effectiveness.  In  organizations  of  this  type,  which\\noperate  in  a  dynamic,  unpredictable  environment,  motivational  elements  tailored  to  the\\nspecifics  of  work  based  on  flexibility,  cooperation,  and  innovation  are  of  particular  value.\\nMotivating  employees  is  not  limited  to  material  aspects,  but  also  includes  a  wide  range  of\\nintangible factors that affect the sense of belonging, professional development, and the ability\\nto fulfill individual ambitions (Sęczkowska, 2021).\\nOne of the key motivational factors is the sense of autonomy in performing assigned tasks\\n(Gadomska-Lila,  2013).  Employees  of  agile  organizations  value  the  possibility  of  making\\nindependent  decisions  and  freedom  of  action,  which  allows  for  greater  creativity  and\\ninnovation.  In  an  environment  based  on  agile  management  methods,  autonomy  strengthens\\nresponsibility for implemented projects and increases team engagement. Employees who have\\nan influence on the decisions made feel more appreciated, which translates into a higher level\\nof motivation (Rosethorn, Mensink, 2008).\\n\\n## [PDF page 213]\\n\\nMotivational factors building the image…  213\\n\\nAn important aspect of motivation is also the opportunity to work in an environment based\\non trust and cooperation (Mayo, 2001). Agile organizations base their functioning on teamwork,\\nwhich requires effective communication and mutual support. A sense of belonging to a team in\\nwhich there is an atmosphere of understanding and respect is one of the key elements building\\nemployee motivation. Thanks to appropriate interpersonal relations, employees have greater\\nsatisfaction with their work, which translates into their loyalty to the organization (Rosário,\\nRaimundo, 2021). Professional development is another factor that is important for motivation\\nin an agile organization. The opportunity to acquire new competences, participate in training\\nand  develop  skills  adapted  to  the  changing  requirements  of  the  labor  market  are\\nan  indispensable  element  of  attracting  and  retaining  talented  employees  (Miś,  2020).\\nOrganizations that offer clear career paths and invest in the development of their staff strengthen\\ntheir  commitment  and  willingness  to  cooperate  long-term.  Employees  then  see  their  future\\nwithin the organization, which significantly affects their motivation to achieve better results\\n(Stuss, 2021).\\nAnother motivational factor is the recognition and appreciation of employees’ work. In agile\\norganizations,  where  quick  results  and  short-term  successes  are  part  of  everyday  life,\\nit is important that the efforts and achievements of teams are regularly noticed and rewarded.\\nAppreciation can take both a formal form, such as awards or bonuses, and an informal form,\\nconsisting of expressing appreciation in everyday communication. This strengthens positive\\nrelationships between employees and superiors and builds an atmosphere of commitment and\\nmotivation (Sajdak, 2021).\\nFlexibility in work,  although often  considered in the context of  work organization, also\\nserves a motivational function. The ability to adjust working hours, work location or tasks in\\na way that meets the individual needs of employees makes the organization perceived as more\\nopen and caring. Employees who have more control over the organization of their working time\\nexperience less stress and a better work-life balance. This in turn affects their productivity and\\nlong-term commitment (Routledge, 2020).\\nMotivation in agile organizations is also the opportunity to take on challenges and test one’s\\nskills in new areas. The dynamic nature of work and the variability of projects are conducive to\\ndeveloping  cognitive  flexibility  and  the  ability  to  learn  quickly.  For  many  employees,  the\\nopportunity to take on new challenges is a source of satisfaction and an opportunity to gain\\nexperience,  which  strengthens  their  sense  of  value  and  professional  competence  (Rahimi,\\nMansouri, 2019).\\nIn  summary,  the  motivational  factors  in  an  agile  organization  go  beyond  traditional\\ncompensation-based models. Autonomy, collaboration, professional development, recognition,\\nflexibility, and the opportunity to take on challenges all play key roles. The interplay of these\\nelements  creates  a  work  environment  that  fosters  employee  engagement,  satisfaction,\\nand loyalty. Agile organizations that can effectively identify and leverage these factors gain\\na competitive advantage by creating a team that can dynamically respond to changing market\\nconditions.\\n\\n## [PDF page 214]\\n\\n214  M. Kocot, K. Olejko\\n\\n1.3.  Motivational factors as a determinant of employer image building in an agile\\norganization\\n\\nMotivational  factors  play  a  key  role  in  building  the  employer’s  image  in  an  agile\\norganization  that  operates  in  a  dynamic,  demanding  environment.  Motivating  employees  in\\nsuch a context becomes not only a tool for improving team effectiveness, but also a foundation\\nfor  strengthening  the  attractiveness  of  the  organization  as  a  workplace  (Lendzion,  2023).\\nEmployees expect not only stability and remuneration, but also conditions that are conducive\\nto  their  development,  health  and  job  satisfaction.  These  activities  are  essential  in  the\\nenvironment of agile organizations, which are characterized by adaptability, cooperation and\\na culture of innovation (Grzybowska, 2022).\\nOne  of  the  key  factors  in  building  the  employer’s  image  is  recognition  and  rewards  for\\nachievements.  Appreciating  the  work  and  effort  of  teams  is  important  for  motivation,  as  it\\nstrengthens  the  sense  of  value  and  affects  the  long-term  commitment  of  employees  (Jones,\\nAdam, 2023). Recognition can take both material forms, such as bonuses or awards, and non-\\nmaterial ones, including expressing gratitude or recognizing achievements in the organization.\\nProperly  implemented  reward  mechanisms  contribute  to  shaping  a  positive  image  of  the\\nemployer,  which  is  perceived  as  an  organization  that  appreciates  the  contribution  of  its\\nemployees (He, Harris, 2021).\\nSkill development opportunities are also an important motivational element, especially in\\nthe environment of agile organizations that require continuous improvement of competencies.\\nEmployees expect access to training, development programs or mentoring that allow them to\\nimprove their qualifications and adapt to changing market requirements. An organization that\\ninvests in employee development is perceived as a modern and responsible employer, which\\nsignificantly  strengthens  its  image  (Kurnia,  Chien,  2020).  Flexible  working  conditions  are\\nanother important motivational factor that is particularly appreciated by modern employees.\\nThe possibility of adjusting working hours, remote or hybrid work and autonomy in carrying\\nout tasks allows for achieving a better work-life balance. Organizations that implement flexible\\nwork models are perceived as more employee-friendly, which naturally affects their image as\\nan attractive place of employment (Matuszewska-Kubicz, 2020).\\nHealth  and  wellness  programs  that  focus  on  the  physical  and  mental  well-being  of\\nemployees  play  an  equally  important  role.  Initiatives  such  as  medical  care,  psychological\\nsupport, or promoting a healthy lifestyle allow employees to feel that their needs are noticed\\nand respected (Fiddler, 2017). An organization that cares about the health and well-being of its\\nteam  builds  the  image  of  a  responsible  employer  that  cares  about  the  well-being  of  its\\nemployees  (Machnicka,  2020).  Integration  activities  are  important  for  building  team\\nrelationships  and  strengthening  an  organizational  culture  based  on  cooperation  and  trust.\\nIn  agile  organizations,  where  teamwork  is  the  foundation  of  action,  joint  initiatives  and\\nintegration activities promote better communication, understanding, and building strong bonds\\n\\n## [PDF page 215]\\n\\nMotivational factors building the image…  215\\n\\nbetween employees. An organization that supports integration is perceived as open and friendly,\\nwhich positively affects its perception as an employer (Oczkowska, 2015).\\nImproving the infrastructure of the workplace is another motivational factor that refers to\\nensuring comfortable and modern conditions for performing duties. Office spaces adapted to\\nthe needs of teams, ergonomic workstations and access to modern tools and technologies affect\\nemployee efficiency and satisfaction. An organization that invests in the development of the\\nwork  environment  strengthens  its  attractiveness  in  the  eyes  of  both  current  and  future\\nemployees (Koch, Schermuly, 2021).\\nCareer development support is also an important element of building the employer image\\nin  an  agile  organization.  Employees  value  organizations  that  offer  opportunities  for\\nadvancement,  clear  career  paths,  and  support  in  achieving  professional  goals.  Building\\nan  environment  in  which  career  development  is  a  priority  promotes  long-term  employee\\nengagement and loyalty to the organization (Luo et al., 2020).\\nThe last important motivational factor is encouraging innovation, which is the foundation\\nof agile organizations. Promoting creativity, openness to new ideas and supporting employee\\ninitiatives allows for building an organizational culture based on innovation. Employees who\\nhave  the  opportunity  to  implement  their  own  ideas  and  influence  the  development  of  the\\norganization  feel  more  motivated  and  appreciated,  which  naturally  strengthens  the  positive\\nimage of the employer (Kulpa-Puczyńska, 2011).\\nIn summary, motivational factors play a key role in building the employer image in an agile\\norganization. Their importance goes beyond the material forms of remuneration, encompassing\\nareas  related  to  development,  health,  work  flexibility  and  innovation.  Organizations  that\\neffectively identify  employee needs and implement consistent motivational strategies create\\na work environment that promotes engagement, loyalty and long-term cooperation, which in\\nturn strengthens their image as attractive employers.\\n\\n1.4.  Research Methodology\\n\\nThe aim of the research was to identify the key determinants of building the employer image\\nin an agile organisation and to determine their impact on the perception of the organisation as\\nan  attractive  place  to  work.  The  research  also  aimed  to  establish  the  relationship  between\\nindividual elements of the employer branding strategy and employee preferences in the context\\nof building a positive employer image. It was assumed that flexible forms of work, the use of\\nmodern technologies, promoting a culture of openness and harmony in the organisation and\\nquick response to employee needs significantly affect the positive perception of the organisation\\nby its current and potential employees.\\nA  research  hypothesis  was  formulated,  according  to  which  key  elements  of  employer\\nbranding, such as flexibility, innovation, openness and quick response to the team’s needs, have\\na  significant  impact  on  building  the  employer’s  image  in  the  environment  of  an  agile\\norganization. Discussion\\n\\nThe conclusions from the conducted research indicate that the determinants of building the\\nemployer image in an agile organization are diverse in terms of their importance and perception\\nby respondents. The key factor turned out to be the flexibility of work forms, which is highly\\nvalued  by  employees  and  plays  a  fundamental  role  in  perceiving  the  organization  as\\nan attractive employer. Flexible forms of work, such as the possibility of remote work, flexible\\nhours  or  adapting  the  work  mode  to  individual  needs,  are  seen  as  an  essential  element\\nsupporting the balance between work and private life, which significantly affects the level of\\nemployee satisfaction and engagement.\\nEqually  important  was  the  use  of  modern  technologies.  Respondents  note  that  these\\ntechnologies  not  only  facilitate  the  organization  of  work  and  communication  in  the  team,\\nbut also increase the efficiency of the tasks performed. The integration of modern tools, such\\nas  project  management  platforms  or  systems  supporting  teamwork,  is  perceived  as\\nan  expression  of  the  organization’s  innovative  approach  and  its  readiness  to  adapt  to  the\\nchanging work environment. This, in turn, builds the image of the organization as a modern and\\nfuture-oriented employer.\\nThe  culture  of  openness  and  harmony  in  the  organization  was  also  highly  rated.\\nRespondents appreciated values such as transparency in communication, mutual respect and\\nsupporting  teamwork.  The  culture  of  openness  helps  build  trust,  increases  the  sense  of\\nbelonging  to  the  organization  and  affects  employee  loyalty.  In  the  environment  of  an  agile\\norganization, where teamwork and quick decision-making are key, this culture turns out to be\\nan indispensable element supporting operational efficiency.\\nA quick and flexible response to employee needs was indicated as another important factor\\nin  building  a  positive  employer  image.  Organizations  that  are  able  to  dynamically  adapt  to\\nemployee expectations are perceived as more caring and responsible. Such activities strengthen\\nteam engagement and influence the positive perception of the organization by both current and\\npotential  employees.  The  ability  to  quickly  solve  problems  and  the  flexibility  to  adapt  to\\nchanging staff needs are key aspects of building positive employee experiences.\\nMultivariate  correspondence  analysis  (MCA)  allowed  for  a  deeper  understanding  of  the\\nrespondents’ response patterns. It was identified that some variables, such as flexibility of work\\nforms and open culture, are closely related, which may indicate their complementarity in the\\nrespondents’ perception. In turn, other variables, such as the use of modern technologies or\\nquick response to employee needs, are perceived as more independent, which emphasizes their\\nunique nature in the employer branding strategy.\\nIn summary, the research results confirm the importance of a comprehensive approach to\\nbuilding  an  employer  image  in  agile  organizations.  Key  determinants  such  as  flexibility,\\ninnovation, openness and responsiveness must be included in employer branding strategies to\\n\\n## [PDF page 220]\\n\\n220  M. Kocot, K. Olejko\\n\\nmeet  the  expectations  of  today’s  employees.  Organizations  that  effectively  integrate  these\\nelements have a better chance of attracting and retaining talented employees, which in the long\\nterm  affects  their  competitiveness  and  ability  to  adapt  to  the  changing  work  environment.\\nThe research conclusions provide valuable advice for organizations that want to effectively\\nbuild their image as an attractive employer in a dynamic and demanding business environment.\\nBased  on  the  conclusions  obtained,  recommendations  can  be  formulated  that  will  help\\ncompanies  effectively  build  an  attractive  employer  image  in  agile  organizations.\\nIt  is  recommended  to  introduce  flexible  forms  of  work  as  the  foundation  of  the  employer\\nbranding strategy. Conclusions\\n\\nComparing the results of research on building the employer image in agile organizations\\nwith the findings of other researchers, one can notice both similarities and differences in the\\nperception  of  the  key  determinants  of  this  process.  Research  conducted  by  Gadomska-Lila\\n(2013) indicated that building the image of a good employer is not a common activity, and in\\nmany companies the area of human resources management contains significant potential for\\ndevelopment in the process of building the image.  In turn, Kusibab (2013) emphasizes that\\nactivities in the field of building the image of an attractive employer have become increasingly\\nused by managers of various organizations in recent years. The author draws attention to the\\nimportance of skillful shaping of the image in a way that attracts the best candidates to the\\ncompany.\\nOczkowska (2015) notes that the process of building an organization’s image as an employer\\nconsists  of  several  stages,  including  shaping  and  consolidating  the  image.  The  author\\nemphasizes that the organization’s image can be built in several ways, depending on previously\\nconducted activities. In the context of flexible forms of employment, research conducted by\\nKulp-Puczyńska (2011) indicates the growing importance of flexibility in the labor market.\\nThe  author  analyzes  the  preparation  of  vocational  school  students  for  flexible  forms  of\\nemployment and work organization, emphasizing the importance of this preparation from the\\npoint of view of employment opportunities in the contemporary labor market.\\nSimilarly,  the  research  presented  by  Oczkowska  (2015)  indicates  different  types  of  the\\nimage  of  an  organization  as  an  employer,  depending  on  the  criteria  taken  into  account.\\nThe author emphasizes that the process of building the image of an organization as an employer\\nconsists of several stages, including shaping and consolidating the created image.
