Introduction\\nCountries  in  Asian  such  as  China,  South  Korea,  Japan,  India,  Malaysia,  Vietman,  Philipine,\\nSingapore and Thailand are usually cited among the fastest growing economies in the world (Lau et\\nal.  2014,  Apergis  &  Ozturk,  2015).  On  the  backyard  of  this growth,  although  these  countries  are\\nclassified among the top  higher technological  products producers with an important part of their\\nprodution exported worlwide, some of them such as China and India are nevertheless usually cited\\namong  the  most  polluters  in  Asian  continent  (Zambrano-Monserrata  et  al.  2018b,  IPCC,  2022),\\nwithout any concern in the past years relative to environmental pollution issues Apergis & Ozturk,\\n2015. Concern related to environmental protection, climate change and pollution mitigation is one\\nof the Asia Pacific region’s main environmental problems. More so, Asia Pacific’s share of global\\nemissions has seen an increase from 5338 millions metric tons of CO2 (MtCO2) in 1990 to 17.9551\\nmillions MtCO2 in 2019 because the region has become a global manufacture hub, and rising middle\\nclass with rising income levels that impacts consumption-based emissions (IPCC, 2022, Low, 2023).\\nAt term in 2022, the increase of emissions level in this region was far more than the combined total\\nemissions  of  all  other  regions  (North  America,  Middle  East,  Africa,  Europe,  South  and  Central\\nAmerica) and China alone accounted for nearly 60% of Asia Pacific carbone missions (Tiseo, 2023).\\n\\nThe headlong rush to economic  growth that characterized Asian countries during these last years\\nraises  four  main  concerns :  the  first  is  directly  related  to  the  needs  of  Natural  Resources  (NRs)\\nwhich is necessary for supporting the rapid increase of the population and economic growth. The\\nsecond is in link with the production diversification patterns (Bustos et al. 2012) that provides an\\nadvantage in export, trade and competitiveness capabilities. The third is resumed in the factors that\\ncan provide insight to predict changes in economic structure (Hausmann et al. 2014). The last point\\nis  about  the  consequent  environmental  degradation  that  comes  parallel  to  this  fast  growth\\n(Zambrano-Monserrate et al. 2016) while raising the questions of environmental goals, sustainability\\nand green achievements.\\n\\nThese four concerns present above are characterizing and defining the Economic Complexity (EC)\\nor  Economic  Sophistication  (ES)  concept  usually  represents  by  the  Economic  Complexity  Index\\n(ECI) (Hausmann et al., 2007, Hidalgo & Hausmann, 2009, Hausmann et al., 2011, Hausmann &\\nHidalgo,  2011).  In  Asian  economies,  the  evolution  of  the  economic  data  used  to  measure  these\\naforementioned  realities  (NRs  consumption,  diversification  capabilities,  comparative  advantage  in\\nproduction and exportation of complex product, environmental challenge) can lead to appreciate the\\nlong run development and sustanaibility achievements coupled with the structural change path. As\\nunderlined  by  Hausmann  et  al.  (2014),  focusing  on  transformation  of  the  economic  structure  is\\nmotivated  by  the  ECI’s  ability  to  explain  and  predict  important  macroeconomic  outcomes,  from\\neconomic growth to the abatement of pollution emissions level and reduction of income inequality\\nchallenges.  Therefore,  the  well-known  inverted  U-Shaped  curve  hypothesis  framework  from\\nGrossman  and  Krueger  (1995)  that  characterises  a  sustainable  relationship  between  economic\\ngrowth,  capabilities,  transformations,  achievements  and  the  environmental  quality  with  the\\ngeneration  of  the  reduction  of  environmental  degradation  can  be  used  as  main  theoretical\\nunderpinning of this research.\\n\\nThe  aforementioned  close  link  between  ECI  and  environmental  improvements  has  received\\nwidespread attention in the literature only within the European context (Laverde-Rojas et al. 2021,\\nNeagu  &  Teodoru,  2019),  in  a  selected world  sample  (Dogan  et al.  2019), or  by  focusing  on  the\\nexportation diversification capabilities (Mania, 2020 ; Apergis et al. 2018, Can & Gozgor, 2017).\\n\\n1 Statista (2023), Statistical Review of World Energy 2023, from Energy Institute.\\n\\n## [PDF page 4]\\n\\nFrom the aforementioned determinant role of NRs to support economic growth (Topcu & Aslan,\\n2020), we  address that issue by including it among the main explanatory control variables. Given\\nthat  it  is  a  particular  issue  with  a  long  history  and  great  significance  in  the  debate  within  the\\nframework of the natural resources curse hypothesis, we therefore use it for controlling the effect of\\nnatural  resources  on  environmental  degradation.  More  so,  we  hypothesizing  that  the  other\\ntransmission  channels  that  can  have  significant  direct  effects  on  the  green  path  development  are\\nthrough environmental regulations with green taxation, energy consumption per capita and pollution\\nthat  comes  from  international  exchange  of  products.  All  these  variables  are  tested  together  to\\ncapture  the  jointly  effect  of  all  the  variables.  The  results  obtained  in  the  baseline  that  aim  at\\nexplaning whether the development path is sustained can be considered as obtained from a jointly\\nrealistic factors.\\n\\nHypothesis: Justification of the study\\nHypothesis 1: Let assume that ESC is an combined factor that efficiently agregated the following\\nindividual factors through the use of an optimal know-how capabilities: energy consumption, natural\\nresources,  economic  complexity,  international  trade,  environmental  regulation  with  tax.  We  know\\nfrom Hidalgo and Hausmann (2009) that ECI accounts for the changes in the economic structure.\\nThis variable is reflecting the high capabilities to produce diverse and less ubiquitous goods and is a\\nhelpful measurement of economic development. Therefore, this study differs from that of Hidalgo\\n& Hausmann as it assumes that ESC combined factor is used as a set of explanatory variables to\\naccount  for  the  changes  in  the  Economic  system  while  evaluating  for  improvements  in\\nenvironmental  quality  in  Asia-Pacific  countries  as  required  in  the  COP28  framework  (less  fossil\\nenergies strategy). In fact, it is assumed here that ECI interact with other variables in the set of the\\nESC components above for targeting an improved environmental quality.\\n\\nHypothesis  2:  Individual  factors  through  which  ESC  can  be  dissociated  are  introduce\\nsimultaneously  to  evaluate  the  environmental  quality  index,  and  can  be  considered  as  additional\\nexplanatory control variables.\\n\\nThis study contributes to number of research areas and presents some implications. First, to the best\\nof  our  knowledge,  there  are  not  previous  studies  that  investigate  the  link  between  changes  in\\neconomic  structure  and  improvements  in  environmental  quality  or  degradation  under  NRs\\nconstraint in Asian-Pacific context. The study closes to the vision developed in this paper is the one\\nof Tchapchet-Tchouto (2023b) that mainly investigated the existence of EKC when controling for\\nNRs, with a particular focus on how NRs and its different components can impact environmental\\nquality.  At  all,  the  study  shows  that  Asia-Pacific  economies  are  on  a  so-called  « green-resilience »\\npath. However, this study differs in twofolds with that previous work : first, regarding the initiative\\nof  decoupling  the  economic  structural  change  through  its  different  mechanism  including  the\\neconomic  sophistication  feature ;  second,  by  using  a  different  econometric  methods,  we  test  the\\nwhole  factors  effect  simultaneously  in  the  Environmental  Kuznets  Curve  framework.  Therefore,\\ntaking advantage of these constributions, this article is filling a gap in the literature, within the Asian-\\nPacific  context.  More  so,  the  approach  developed  in  this  paper  differs  in  two  strands  from  the\\nprevious  studies  that  are  within  the  scope  of  the  investigation  of  the  green  development  path\\nhypothesis:  indeed,  we  contribute  to  the  literature  by  initially  documenting  a  strong  relationship\\nbetween  sustainable  environmental  quality  indicators  and  economic  growth  with  ECI  among  the\\nexplanatory variables on one hand. This consistent result is the first that aims at evaluating ECI as\\nwell  as  other  structural  change  factors  effects  with  Environmental  Kuznets  Curve  framework  in\\nAsian-Pacific context. On a  second hand, we continue  by estimating the effect of total NRs, and\\nafter  that  we  verify  if  the  sustainable  development  path  holds  when  controlling  for  each  natural\\nresources rents component (oil, mineral, gas and forest rents).\\n\\n## [PDF page 5]\\n\\nThird,  compared  with  other  studies  that  had  focused  on  Environmental  Kuznets  Curve  in  the\\ncontext  of  Asian-Pacific  countries,  we  used  the  most  recent  data  length  available  at  this  stage  to\\nconduct our research. (2020) and\\nZambrano-Monserrata et al. (2018a) jointly found that NRs exhacerbated environmental quality by\\nincreasing GHG emissions in Asian countries.\\n\\nTaguchi (2013) used Generalized Method of Moments to estimate the effects of carbon emission\\nand sulfure in 19 Asian countries for the period 1950-2009. The results show that w hile  carbon\\nemissions increase along the pathway of the per capita GDP, sulfur emissions follow the inverted U-\\nShaped. In Malaysia,  Lau et al. (2014) have  investigated for the period  1979-2008,  the relationship\\nbetween  carbon  emissions  and  per  capita  income  using  bounds  testing  approach  and  Granger\\ncausality estimation technique. They found as result that the development of the economy is linked\\nin short and long run, with the lower level of carbon emissions. Zambrano-Monserrata et al. (2018b)\\nhave tested the Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis in Singapore from data spanning 1971 –\\n2011  with  Granger  causality  and  autoregressive  distributed  lag  bound  testing  methods.  The  study\\nconfirms  in  both  short  and  long  term,  the  existence  of  an  inverted  U-Shaped.  Lee  et  al.  (2021)\\nestablished with ARDL that Environmental Kuznets Curve hypothesis is verified in China from data\\nspanning the period 2002-2018.\\n\\nUsing Generalized Method of Moments estimation strategy, Apergis and Ozturk (2015) investigate\\nthe  relationship  between environmental  degradation  and  GDP  per  capita  in  14  Asian  economies.\\nWith data spanning from 1990-2011, the results show a sustainable path in favour of an inverted U-\\n\\n## [PDF page 6]\\n\\nShaped. Results, robustness tests and discussion\\n4.1.  Results\\nThis section is organized in two parts: The first deals with the baseline empirical results, the second\\npresents  sensitivity  analysis  results  of  the  baseline  findings.  Both  parts  contain  some  elements  of\\ndiscussion.\\n\\nThe  Table  3  presents  the  baseline  results of  the  green  path  development  under  structural  change\\nhypothesis and NRs constraints. The results reveal that Asia-Pacific countries are on the path of a\\nsustainable development regarding the signs and significativity of the coefficients that characterized\\nthe economic development variable. Figure 1 illustrates how the estimated trend of the point cloud\\ndescribes a quadratic function. By adjusting the per capita carbon emission index variable to the per\\ncapita GDP, the econometric methods based on different estimation techniques (OLS estimations,\\ntwo-step system GMM, Driscoll-Kraay estimation and panel quantile regression) show the evidence\\nthat  the  Asia-Pacific  environmental  curve  corresponds  to  a  specific  polynomic  association  or\\ninverted U-Shaped as demonstrated by Grossman and Krueger (1995) after Kuznets (1955).\\n\\nAfter  a  first  test  with  total  NRs  rents,  different  specifications  are  performed  with  each  natural\\nresource  component  (oil,  gas,  mineral  and  forest  rents)  [columns  (2  to  5)]  and  with  all  these\\n\\n## [PDF page 10]\\n\\ncomponents  together  [column  (6)].  The  effect  of  total  NRs  on  the  level  of  hamful  pollution  is\\npositive and strongly significant at 1% level. This result is consistent with the findings of Kuo et al.\\n(2022). More so, under the jointly effects of the other characterized factors which derive from the\\ndecomposition of the structural change phenomenon, the relationship between variables are strongly\\nconfirming  the  inverted  U-Shaped  form  in  the  different  specifications  of  NRs.  These  results\\nevidenced that GDP coefficients are all positive and strongly significant at 1% level. Morever, it can\\nbe seen from the results given by the Table 4 that represents a first robustness with Ecofootprint\\nIndex as an alternative mesure of the green path development, that the baseline results are robust\\nunder this alternative variable econometric analysis. Table 4 highlights that ECI effect is significant\\nin  column  [2,  4,  6]  and  always  positive  as  similar  in  Table  3.  From  both  baseline  and  alternative\\ndependent  variable  sensitivity  tests,  we  also  find  that  NRs seem  to  have  a  negative  effect  on  the\\ngreen path development mostly through oil consumption than other natural resources components.\\nMeanwhile, the rationale that can explain the results in whole could be the following : the leveraging\\neffects  of  clean  improvements  that  come  from  all  the  other  factors,  greenest  achievements  and\\nstrenghts  from  leadership  in  environmental  policies  of  the  Asia-Pacific  context  are  helping  to\\nmaintain  a  sustainable  development  path.  So,  pollution  degradation  obtains  from  international\\nmovement of knowledge, technology, exchanging sophisticated good between countries and change\\nin the economic  structure, yield to a sustainable path. This is consistent with  Tchapchet-Tchouto\\n(2023b). Likewise, energy consuption is found to significantly harm the green development and the\\nresult is consitent with Chen et al. (2019). Consistent with Saucedo et al. (2017), environmental tax\\nsignificantly improve the green development path. However, international trade is detrimental to the\\nenvironmental quality and the finding is opposite to that of Awan et al. Sensitivity analysis\\nRegarding  the  OLS  limits  discussed  before,  the  two-step  system  GMM  estimation  strategic  and\\npanel  quantile  regression  are  used  to  reinforce  the  power  of  the  baseline  findings.  Results  are\\ndisplayed in Table 5. Regarding the Hansen test results, this empirical analysis demonstrates that the\\nmodel estimated through the two-step system GMM is not over-identified. More so, regarding the\\nSargan test of overidentifying  restriction, instruments are valid, exogeneity conditions is valid and\\nuncorrelated with the error term. The diagnostic test also shows that the number of instruments is\\nlower that the total number of observations, P-value of the AR(1) is significant and nearly equal to 0,\\nand AR(2) is up to the prescribed limit of significancy.  The AR(2) results suggest that the  model\\ndoest not suffer from second order serial autocorrelation. The lagged dependent variable is positive\\nand strongly significant at 1%. This finding reveals that the past level of pollution emission have an\\ninfluence on the current level of pollution.\\n\\nLikewise,  Pooled  OLS  executed  with  Driscoll-Kraay  estimation  method,  and  the  non-parametric\\nestimation  method  that  is  panel  QR  (Koenker  &  Bassett,  1978)  are  realized  in  further  sensitivity\\nsteps  and  results  are  presented  in  Table  6.  From  the  Pooled  OLS,  we  also  introduce  additional\\ncontrol variables that strenghten the estimated results and keep them in the QR analysis. Different\\nhypothesis are therefore examined with the introduction of FDI inflows, R&D, inflation as well as\\nthe use of internet by the population. Before discussing the effect of introducing additional control\\nvariables, it should also be noted that the main appeal of using QR it that this methodology is more\\nrobust than OLS in that it is less affected by outliers in data than least-squared regression. More so,\\nQR  gives  informations  about  the  shape  of  a  distribution,  in  particular  whether  a  distribution  is\\nskewed or not. The interest is to determine a causal relationship beyond the mean-to-mean effects.\\nPooled OLS with additional control variables as well as 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th quantiles are\\nconsistent  with  the  previous  estimates.  A  comparative  analysis  reveals  that  the  results  are\\nheterogeneous among different quantiles and that upper quantiles (75th and 90th) are the ones that\\npresent the most higher GDP coefficients. Conclusion\\nStructural  transformation,  green  economic  expansion  and  great  improvements  in  sustainability\\nchallenges  are  at  the  core  of  Sustainable  Development  Goals  in  the  context  of  fast-growing\\ncountries such as Asia-Pacific economies. The on-hand study is an effort to explore how green is the\\npath of their economic development by proposing an interpretation of the structural transformation\\ndecomposition through its main characteristics: the implication of economic complexity that set up\\nthe  importance  of  the  need  for  factors  that  can  predict  change  in  economic  structure  such  as\\nknowledge process, diversification and technological sophistication (1), NRs that support economic\\nexpansion  and  population  growth  (2),  energy consumption  dimension  (3),  international  trade  that\\naccounts  for  competitiveness  capabilities  and  also  exchange  of  sophisticated  goods  between\\ncountries, international movement of technology (4), and the challenge that goes beyond economic\\ngrowth  to  the  decrease  of  environmental  degradation.  To  achieve  this  objective,  this  study  has\\nutilized the quadratic framework developed by  Kuznets (1955) and popularized by Grossman and\\nKrueger (1995) to bridge the  research gap. In doing so with this demonstration, this study  draws\\nnovel  contributions  and  implications  regarding  the  sustainable  growth  path.
